zh: 手机暗下去之前，Adrian又碰了一下屏幕。那张照片重新亮起。
Roman的胸口被一个红色圆点压住。照片没拍到持枪的人，也没写拍摄时间。
Adrian两指一分，像素把衣料撕成一块一块，什么都证明不了。那一点红却始终压在同一个位置，像一颗随时会炸开的痣。
他盯着那一点，掌心先烫了起来。他把脸埋进过那片胸口，听过布料底下的心跳，在飞机颠簸时被整个人按进那片温度里。
照片上的红点和记忆里的热叠在一起，胃里一阵发紧。危险本该让人冷静，身体却先一步拒绝了冷静。
我现在需要他活着。至于我还想从他身上要什么，可以晚一点再算。
门外传来很轻的一声。电梯到层了。
今天早晨，他还以为最难对付的是老板那条“中午前改完稿”的消息。现在他站在一间不属于他记忆的玄关里，地毯厚得踩不出声音，门锁旁的小屏幕却把走廊放得清清楚楚。
Roman站在电梯左边。同一件深色衬衫，同一道没抚平的袖口折痕。肩线把布料撑得很满，呼吸时胸膛有极轻的起伏。
活着的人比照片多出一口呼吸——也多出一具会发热、会紧绷、会因为紧张而微微挪动重心的身体。
Adrian盯着那点起伏，忽然厌恶起自己的眼睛。它竟然还记得Roman转身时腰线先动、肩膀才跟上；记得领口露出来的那截锁骨，在灯下会显得更浅。
危险没有让吸引消失，只让它更难承认——像藏在袖口里的一块烫伤，一碰就疼，却总忍不住伸手确认它还在不在。
Adrian看了看自己站的位置。他根本不在窗边。这句太熟练的命令，让那点恐惧一下子有了可以发火的方向。Roman的声音是从胸腔里压出来的，低、稳，带着一点被按住的沙哑。
先确认你自己。你现在站在哪儿？
Roman抬头，看向门口的摄像头，没假装不知道自己被看着。镜头里，他的下颌绷得很紧，喉结因为吞咽轻轻滚了一下。
东侧电梯前。左边是实体墙，右边通服务走廊。
直到出口和通道核对完。
Roman按住耳机，报出值班台的工号，嗓音里那点胸腔的共鸣顺着耳机震进耳膜。Adrian在门锁屏上找到了同一个号码——今晚第一次，有一个回答可以在Roman之外找到对应。
你也别站在那儿证明你能保护我。
Roman没立刻接话。门镜里，他垂在身侧的手慢慢松开，指节因为刚才攥得太紧还泛着白，一点一点恢复血色。
Adrian盯着那只手。它按过他的腰侧，扣过他的手腕，在飞机颠簸时把他整个人拽进怀里。记忆里的触感，比眼前的危险先一步爬上了脊背。

then: Roman的手机在镜头边缘亮着，屏幕上是Adrian转过去的那张照片。红点压在他胸口——和现实里那具还在呼吸的身体重合在一起。
原消息留着，别裁剪。我已经让保全调了对应时段的录像。
所以你收到了，还往电梯走？
我在撤回路线上。你看到的，是我停下来等通道确认。
他把身体又往实体墙上贴近了一点。衬衫被墙面压出一道浅痕，肩背的轮廓反而更清楚了。
Roman听见了“进来”，却没有把它当成原谅。他的喉结动了一下，像把什么话咽了回去。

then.why: 他第一时间把威胁发给了Roman

then: 说完，他的左手不自觉地攥住了右腕。门外，Roman的目光落在摄像头上，很稳——稳得让Adrian觉得自己被看穿了。不是谎话被看穿，是那点想一个人把危险挡在门外的冲动被看穿了。
没有。我正在问我不知道的那一部分。
这句话来得太晚。可Adrian也知道，自己正在做同一种事。他把照片转给值班台，抄送Roman。消息发出去，手腕才松开，指腹上还留着自己掐出来的浅印。
我想让你离危险远一点。
你可以要求我离开。别替我删掉判断要用的东西。
Roman低头看了一眼收到的图。镜头里，他的下颌收紧，肩线绷了一瞬，又逼着自己放松。
他的声音冷了一点。工作指令一条不少，私人的那一部分没有跟着回来。Adrian盯着屏幕，忽然很想伸手穿过门板，去碰一碰那截被冷意压住的温度。

then.why: 他差点又一个人扛

then: 值班台的通知盖住了照片：内部通道存在异常访问，范围尚未确认。
不是凶手的名字，也不是“这栋楼里的人都可信”的保证。Adrian的手指在屏幕边缘收紧，指节发白。
我已经查过一次来源。它走的是内部通道。
Adrian报出记录号。Roman把同一个号码复述了一遍——没让他撤回，也没夸他抓到了谁。镜头里，Roman的呼吸明显沉了一拍，像把怒气压回了胸腔。
别再扩大共享。先保住这份记录。
你是想让我把手机交出来？
不。我要另一份独立副本。
Adrian把手机留在自己掌心，按下导出。这栋楼里终于有一样东西，不必因为被叫作Vale的财产，就交到Vale的人手里。
可他仍能感觉到Roman的目光隔着镜头落在他手上——沉得像要隔着门板把人拽过去。

then.why: 追踪指向Vale内部

else: Adrian往下滑了一下屏幕。便利店门口。塑料袋。少年Roman朝镜头伸过来的手。照片背面那句话还在：“他本来就不该回来找你。”
他忽然不想把这张照片给任何人看。不是因为里面藏着多大的秘密——是有人把他珍惜过的东西拿出来，证明自己连那一小块地方也进得去。
照片里的Roman肩背还没完全长开，已经看得出后来会撑满衬衫的轮廓。
他们有我们那张旧照片。
Roman的脸在镜头里变了。很短，却足够Adrian看清——下颌绷紧，眼神暗了一瞬，像被什么从里面击中。
你拿着两杯饮料。我那杯还没打开。
Roman垂了一下眼。镜头里能看见他睫毛的影子，和领口随呼吸起伏的那道弧。
原消息先留着。那张照片为什么会在他们手里，我也要查。
你不记得我喝什么，倒记得是哪一张？
我记得你没喝。你那天一直在等我把话说完。
Adrian关掉照片，胸腔里有什么轻轻撞了一下。
门外的人没有给出十年前给不出的答案，只是把自己的位置又报了一遍。Adrian盯着屏幕里那具还活着的身体，清楚地意识到：危险让他更想碰他，而不是更想逃。

zh.hint: 门锁屏上，他的手停在开关上方。门外那个人在等你一句话——让他退，让他进，还是先别挂？

opts.t: 别替我安排。把路线说清楚。
then: Adrian把手机竖在门锁屏旁边。两个画面一起亮着，他才发现自己刚才一直只看Roman，没看他身后的走廊。
镜头右边看不到。那里有什么？
服务间。从你那一头，没法确认里面没人。
所以不是我看见你安全，你就安全。
一个字，把他那点想靠自己解决一切的冲动压了下去。他让值班台先说明已核验的退回路线，再要Roman复述下一步——没有术语，只有从哪儿走、什么时候停、谁来确认。
Roman按说明退到实体墙后。那个宽阔的身影从画面里消失的一瞬，Adrian的手一下收紧。他几乎又要叫他回来——不是因为害怕，是那具身体离开画面的那一秒，胸口空了一块。
已到内侧安全区。没进服务间。
那一声从耳机里直接顶进耳膜，低、稳，带着胸腔的震动。Adrian按着说话键，闭了闭眼，让那三个字在耳道里多停了半秒。他没有开门，也第一次没把关着的门当成“我什么都做不了”的证明。
opts.rthink: 他问的是路线，不是我。……这样更好。他终于不再替我挡在门口了。

opts.t: 今晚别进来。把接班的人叫到值班台。
then: 是今晚不进这间屋，还是不再负责你的私人安保？
前一个。后一个，明天书面谈。
问得这么准，让Adrian更难接着生气。好像连拒绝，也得被Roman接得体体面面，才算数。
你不用表现得这么理解我。
Roman侧过头，叫接班人员去值班台报到，把工号发过来。Adrian手机上没有一长串解释，只有交接地点、确认时间、下一次安全通知。
那几行字比任何一句“我担心你”都冷，也更让人想伸手碰一碰说话的人。
问出口，他就后悔了。Roman却没有顺着这句话走回门口。
你让我今晚别进来。我照做。
电梯门重新打开。金属门一点一点挡住那个熟悉的肩膀，衬衫在灯下最后亮了一下，没了。他要的是距离。真拿到了，身体却不高兴——像有人把一截正在发热的东西从掌心里抽走，只剩空，和痒。
他把手机贴在冰凉的门板上，过了很久才收回来。门板的凉，压不住指尖的热。
opts.rthink: 他说“今晚”。不是“以后”。……我听得出区别。我就在楼下，哪儿也不去。

opts.t: 确认完通道再进来。今晚别碰我。
then: 门锁屏跳出通道确认。Adrian先向值班台复核了一遍，才解开门链。
门链滑开的一瞬，夜风的凉先涌进来，紧跟着是Roman身上的味道——枪油、须后水，和一点因为紧张渗出来的汗。Adrian下意识吸了一口气，胸口一紧。
Roman站得比他预想的远，皮鞋停在玄关地毯的边线外。衬衫领口有一道被耳机线磨出来的折痕，下颌的阴影压得很低。刚才在耳机里冷静的声音，到了这个距离，有了胸腔。
近处的Roman总比屏幕里更难对付——肩背更宽，呼吸更沉，眼睛里压着的东西也更重。Adrian退开一步。
Roman等他让出路线，才走进来；经过时肩膀从他身侧擦过，布料相触的一瞬，两个人都绷了一下，谁也没回头。
Roman走到厨房岛台另一边。不伸手，不挡出口。可两人之间那截刻意留出来的空白，已经热得像有人在中间烧了一根线。
opts.rthink: “别碰我。”他说这句的时候，看的是我的手。……我会把手放在他看得见的地方。

opts.t: 我现在说不出完整的话。先别挂。
then: Adrian背贴上门。他一直在发指令、问问题，好像只要有一件事还在他手里安排，今晚就不会退回十年前那个没人回消息的夜里。现在他忽然没话了。胸口发紧，像有人隔着皮肉按住了他的呼吸。
没有“冷静”，没有“相信我”。耳机里只有很轻的衣料声，和他向值班台确认退回位置的声音。Adrian顺着门板坐到地上。地毯很软，软得让他更生气。
Roman的呼吸停了一瞬。耳机里那一瞬的安静，比任何解释都清楚。
Adrian抹了一把脸，指尖是干的。他没哭，这也没让他好受多少。通道确认后，Roman问他要不要先让值班员上来；Adrian选了值班员。Roman在通话里一直等到对方抵达，才挂断。
手机还在他手里。掌心却烫得厉害，像刚刚隔着电波，握住了什么不该握的东西。
opts.rthink: 他说“先别挂”。十年前我挂掉的那通电话，他记到现在。这次我等到最后一秒。

then: 四十分钟后，值班台推来一条加急通知：东侧楼顶确认有人停留过，顶层封锁升级。接班的人被堵在地库安检。按规程，最近的持证护卫要进屋。
门铃没响。门锁屏上，Roman站在地毯边线外，手垂在身侧，等他。
Adrian看了那张脸很久，按下了开锁。

zh: 落地窗自动落锁，厚重的窗帘一幅一幅降下来。屋里只剩中央空调的低鸣，和两个人还没平下去的呼吸。
Roman检查完最后一扇窗，转身时衬衫被动作扯紧，肩背和腰线的轮廓在低光里清楚得过分。袖口卷到手肘，前臂的青筋随着动作起伏。一滴汗从额角滑到下颌，又没进领口。
Adrian靠在岛台边看着他。危险还没过去，身体却先给出了反应——不是怕，是想再靠近一点。像有人在皮肤底下轻轻推了他一把。
Roman走到他面前，停在一步之外。不更近，也不更远。刚好让Adrian闻得到他身上的味道，看得清领口那截随着呼吸起伏的皮肤。
从现在开始，对外通讯只走加密线路。你手机上会多一个威胁看板。

zh.title: THREAT LEVEL：HIGH
zh.txt: 防护已启动 · 新增：内部门禁日志 / 静默求救信号

zh: Adrian没看屏幕。他在看Roman垂在身侧的手——刚松开过，指节回了血色，还带着用过力的紧。他很想伸手碰碰那截手腕，确认脉搏还在跳。
他没动。Roman却看见了他的视线，喉结轻轻滚了一下。
今晚你不开门，也可以。你让我退，我也会退。但你要知道——我退的不是责任，是距离。
Adrian抬眼。两人之间那一步的空白，忽然烫得厉害。

t: roman
他看我的手。他每次害怕，都看我的手，好像只要它还在动，我就还活着。……那就让他看。

zh: 争吵来得很快。焦点不是威胁本身，是谁有权替谁做决定。
Roman坚持他必须接受完整的安保安排；Adrian不肯被锁进一个用“保护”包装起来的笼子。两个人声音都不高，空气却紧得像要裂开。
Roman站在岛台另一侧，衬衫最上面那颗扣子不知什么时候松了，锁骨的线条在低光里很清楚。灯光落在他下颌上，那道线因为咬紧而微微鼓着，手背上的青筋一路绷到前臂。
Adrian盯着那一点，生气和想碰他的冲动缠在一起，分不开。岛台成了唯一的屏障——没有它，他不确定自己会不会绕过去，用碰代替下一句质问。
你消失十年。现在却用命令的方式站在我面前。
我用命令，是因为我没有别的办法保证你活着。
那你保证过什么？十年前，你保证过什么？
Roman的呼吸沉了一拍。下颌绷紧，肩线微微前压，像身体比嘴更早进入了戒备。

zh.hint: 他在等你回答“十年前保证过什么”。你可以继续逼问，可以说实话——也可以不说话。

opts.t: 回答我。一个一个答，别拿“保护”糊弄过去。
then: Adrian把问题一个接一个抛过去，不给Roman用“保护”重新命名过去的机会。
那天晚上你去哪儿了？谁让你走的？你走之前，想过给我打一个电话吗？
Roman的回答越来越短，眼神却越来越沉。争吵停下来的时候，两人之间的空气冷得发烫——不是温度，是压着的东西。
opts.rthink: 每个问题都打在同一个地方。我答得越短，他越知道我在躲。……他一直都知道。

opts.t: ……我怕。怕你又消失。
then: 我怕。怕你再消失，怕我又站在一个没人回消息的晚上。
说完，他往前走了半步。Roman的身体明显僵了一下，却没有退。Adrian的额头几乎碰到他的下颌，能感觉到对方的呼吸落在自己嘴唇上，热的。
Roman的手抬起来，停在半空。最后只是极轻地落在Adrian手臂外侧，像碰到了电，又收回去。
……别这样。我现在碰你，就停不下来。
opts.rthink: 他说他怕。十年里我设想过他恨我、忘了我，唯独没想过他会怕。我的手停在半空，是因为再往前一寸，我就不配说“保护”两个字了。

opts.t: *他不再争辩，伸手解开Roman衬衫的第二颗扣子。*
then: Adrian不再争辩。他伸手解开Roman衬衫的第二颗扣子，指尖擦过锁骨，再往下，停在胸口。皮肤底下的肌肉瞬间绷紧。
Roman的呼吸沉得发哑。他攥住Adrian的手腕，却没有拉开——反而把那只手更用力地按在自己胸口，按在那颗跳得发疯的心上。
下一秒，后腰抵上了岛台边沿。Roman的吻又深又重，带着十年没说出口的东西压下来；掌心贴着他的腰侧，拇指按进腰窝，力道大得几乎要留下指印。两个人的身体贴得太近，什么反应都藏不住。
可他在真正越线之前停住了。额头抵着Adrian的额头，呼吸乱得厉害。
投票结束之前……我不能失控。
Adrian故意又往前贴了一下。Roman低骂了一声，把人整个按进怀里，下巴抵着他的发顶，很久都没松开。
下次再敢用这种方式打断我，后果你自己负责。

then.title: 岛台边的十分钟
then.teaser: 他说“不能失控”，手却没松开。灯灭之前的那十分钟，只有你们两个知道。
then: 窗帘落得严严实实，整座城被关在外面。顶层只剩空调低低的嗡鸣，和两个人乱成一团的呼吸。
Roman把他抵在岛台边，吻从嘴唇落到下颌，再落到颈侧那道跳得最快的脉上。每一下都很慢，像在确认他还活着。
衬衫的扣子一颗一颗松开，掌心贴上皮肤的那一刻，两个人都抖了一下。十年攒下的东西，在这十分钟里全都找到了出口。
后来的事，灯光记不清。只记得Roman一直没松开他的手，十指扣着，指节抵着冰凉的台面；只记得最后那一下，Roman把脸埋在他颈窝里，叫了他的名字，嗓音哑得不像他。
很久以后，Roman才抬起头，替他把衬衫领口一点点拢好，指腹在他锁骨上停了停。
……上一次我没骗你。这一次，我在骗我自己。

opts.rthink: 他解我扣子的手指在抖。他以为我没发现。我按住那只手，不是为了拦他——是怕他发现，我抖得比他还厉害。

zh: 争吵停了，顶层的空气却没有马上冷下来。空调把温度压得很稳，Adrian的皮肤还是热的——是刚才那些话、那些没碰到或碰到了的地方留下的热，像被按进了皮下，一时散不掉。
Roman站在岛台另一侧，最上面两颗扣子都松着，汗从颈侧滑进领口。他没急着整理自己，像默认Adrian有权看见这些。
因为一旦过线，我就不会再给你机会说“今晚别碰我”。
声音低，带着一点哑。Adrian听得见他胸腔里的震动。两个人对视了几秒，空气里全是没做完的事和没说清的危险。
Roman最终还是把扣子一颗颗扣回去，动作很慢，像在给Adrian最后看一眼的时间。扣到第二颗时，手指顿了一下，才接着扣。
去换衣服。今晚还有一道门要过。

zh.title: Vale欢迎酒会 · 今晚11点
zh.txt: 董事会临时决定今晚为继承人举行欢迎酒会。地点：Vale酒店主厅。你的名字已经在邀请名单上——两次。

zh: Adrian转身时，能感觉到那道目光落在自己后腰上。不躲，也不再往前。像一把收进鞘里的刀，刃口还烫着。
封锁完成后，顶层只剩空调的低鸣，和两个人还没完全平复的呼吸。
Roman检查完最后一轮门窗，衬衫被汗浸湿了一点，贴在肩背和胸口。他走到岛台边，什么也没说，只把一瓶水推到Adrian面前。手指在瓶身上多停了半秒，像在确认自己还有没有资格靠近。
Adrian接过水，指尖擦过Roman的指节。两个人都顿了一下。
你刚才在走廊里，心率很高。
Roman的喉结滚了一下。他没退，也没再往前。两人之间那一步的空白热得发烫。
今晚要是还有下一轮，我希望你先选活着，再选对错。
说完这句，他的目光在Adrian嘴唇上停了一瞬，才逼着自己移开。

zh.txt: 我不是不想说完。是一说完，你就会知道我欠你的比你以为的多。

zh: 造型师推进来三套衣服：深色正装、白色礼服，还有那件Adrian坚持留下的旧外套。镜子占了一整面墙，灯从镜框四周打出来，亮得照不出影子。
Roman站在三步外，手臂交叠，下颌微收。目光却没收——它从Adrian的后颈滑到肩胛，落到被衬衫收紧的腰线，最后极克制地抬回眼睛。只有两秒，足够让Adrian的耳尖发热。
“这套活动空间够吗？”造型师问。
他回答的时候，看的是镜子里的Roman。Roman没有移开视线，只极轻地吐出一口气，像在把什么压回去，胸口的起伏因此明显了一瞬。
Adrian故意抬手去整理袖口，让衬衫下摆往上缩了半寸，露出一截腰侧的皮肤。镜子里，Roman的喉结滚动了，手指在手臂上收紧，指节发白。
（压低声音，只够他听见）看够了吗？
（同样低）没有。所以你最好快点穿好。
语气像命令，尾音却是哑的。Adrian的膝盖软了一下。镜子里，Roman的眼神在那一秒沉得更深，然后硬生生转向门口，像在用职责把自己钉在安全距离外。

t: roman
他是故意的。他十七岁就会这一招，借我的外套，袖子长出一截，偏要在我面前一圈一圈地卷。……我当年就没撑住。

zh.title: 今晚的衣服
zh.hint: 三套衣服挂在镜子前。今晚会有镜头，会有董事，会有一道“错误的门”。你想以什么样子走进去？

then: Adrian扣到最后一颗，嫌太紧，又解开了。镜子里，Roman的目光跟着那一小片颈侧移动，随即克制地抬了回来。
Adrian的手在领口停了一下。没有谁被允许把这个玩笑变成伸手。可空气里的热，已经够清楚了。
Roman先看了他一眼，像在确认这是允许，才走过来。他只扶住袖口，指腹擦过腕骨的那一下，两个人都绷紧了。他指腹上有一层薄茧，克制过的力道还是漏出来一点。
Roman的呼吸落在他耳侧，低得几乎像叹气。袖口整理好了，腕骨上还留着被碰过的感觉，像一枚看不见的印。
这一枚不会替你签任何东西。
造型师确认口袋没破、鞋适合走路，把旧外套的领子刷干净。Adrian穿上时，布料在肩上轻轻牵了一下——是他自己的东西。
Roman看着那件旧衣服，眼神很复杂，像看见了十年前那个还敢在便利店门口等他的人。
我不用看起来像他们，才有资格问问题。
他的声音很低，带着一点几乎被压住的疼。

zh: 车上，Roman又坐在了他身侧，而不是前排。车窗外下起了细雨，城市的灯被拉成一条条湿漉漉的光。
两个人的膝盖从一开始就贴着。布料相触的温度很清楚。每次转弯，大腿会压得更用力一点。Adrian没移开，Roman也没有，像默认这截接触是今晚少数被允许的东西。

zh.hint: 他的手就放在你旁边，隔着一层布料都能感觉到体温。车里很暗，前排的人看不见。你的手——

opts.t: *极轻地覆上他的手背，拇指慢慢摩挲。*
then: 过了两分钟，Roman的手指动了动，极轻地覆上Adrian的手背。没有十指相扣，只是掌心的温度贴上来。拇指在他手侧慢慢地摩挲——一下，停半秒，再一下。像在数脉搏，又像在说：我在。
opts.rthink: 他的手盖上来了。……我没抽开。我等这只手，等了十年。

opts.t: *手留在自己膝盖上，只让膝盖贴着他。*
then: Roman的手一直放在自己膝盖上，指节绷着，一动不动。只有贴着Adrian的那截膝盖，在每次转弯时压得更紧一点。
Adrian低头看了一眼那只克制得发白的手，忽然自己伸过去，覆在了上面。
opts.rthink: 他在忍。手绷成那样，还以为我看不出来。……那就我来。

opts.t: （低声）冷吗？
then: Roman没信。他的手覆上来，掌心贴着Adrian的手背，拇指慢慢摩挲——一下，停半秒，再一下。
opts.rthink: 他问我冷不冷。他明明知道我不冷。……他只是需要一个理由。

zh: Adrian盯着窗外飞快后退的灯。Roman的体温从手背一路爬上手臂，蔓延到颈侧。他什么也没说，Roman也没有。黑暗里，只有膝盖和手的触碰在持续发热。
如果今晚有人真的动手，你打算挡在我前面？
你有没有想过，我不想再看你流血？
想过。所以我会尽量让血留在该留的地方。
说完，拇指在他手背上按得更重了一点。Adrian侧过头，看见他下颌的线条绷得很紧，领口随着呼吸起伏。
直到Adrian的呼吸乱了一拍，那根拇指才停下来——却没有收回手。

zh.why: 车里那只手没有收回去

zh: 酒店门厅里的花比人先得到照顾。花瓣上的水珠还没干，门外排队的人已经等了十分钟。Adrian的名字在记者嘴里叫得很顺，到了门卫的设备上，却显示“待确认”。
他没有掏黑卡解决问题。他先要求核对两张入场码的签发来源：一张来自官方接收渠道；另一张让他走服务层，理由是“避开媒体”。
有人知道我的名字，不等于他的邀请有效。
门卫看了一眼服务层的指示牌，脸色变了。Adrian让他把这个发现写进记录。
门厅的镜面里，Roman站在他身后，守着约好的距离，目光却一直锁在他身上——像一只无形的手，按在他后腰。

zh.title: 有人为你留了一道错误的门
zh.txt: 第二张入场码把你引向服务层的装卸通道。那里没有镜头，也没有记者。

zh.hint: 两张邀请都写着你的名字。只有一张是真的。你从哪一道门进去？

opts.t: 走主入口。我等实名复核。
then: Adrian站在镜头拍得到的位置，要求经理说明正在核验什么。复核通过后，他才往前走。快门声密得像雨。
Roman在他侧后方半步。闪光灯压过来的时候，他的手会落到Adrian后腰——不是挽着，不是宣示给谁看，只是掌心完整地贴上来，五指微微收紧，停两秒。
那只手的拇指有一次刚好按在腰窝。Adrian的呼吸一下乱了。他没回头，只是肩胛绷紧。Roman像察觉到了，力道立刻调整，却没有马上松开。
手移开以后，那一小块皮肤还烫着，凉不下来。
opts.rthink: 他的腰在我手底下绷了一下。……我该松手。我晚了两秒。

opts.t: 走法律通道。合法登记，谁也挑不出错。
then: 法律席确认了他的临时通行资格。Sienna提交完资料，退到顾问的位置，冲他点了一下头，像一个早就预料到他会这么选的人。
Adrian走过核验线时，Roman的目光从另一侧追过来——沉、热，带着明显的不满，又被他自己压住。
opts.rthink: 他选了她递过来的那条路。程序上无可挑剔。……我不喜欢的不是程序。

opts.t: 不进去。我在外面，远程陈述。
then: Adrian停在已确认安全的外部会客区，法律席为他安排了远程陈述。主厅的直播打开时，他的脸出现在大屏幕上。
那声音低得发哑，像直接贴在他耳廓上说的。
opts.rthink: 他不进去，我就不用在两百个人里找那个拿刀的。……他是为了我选的这条路吗？我不敢问。

zh: 接收室的长桌窄得摆不下一顿漂亮的晚餐，却够摆下三份不漂亮的文件。
Sienna把第三页翻开。担保。关联投票。那份婚约，被写成“两家关系稳定”的说明。她指甲上的裸色甲油剥了一小块，她自己大概还没发现。
文件证明不了婚约有效，却能解释，为什么有人宁愿它看起来有效。
这是我这一边，原本想拿到的好处。
不先讲讲其他人会有多惨？
Adrian往下翻。员工、退休安排、融资责任，排在后面。Sienna把副本交给接收人员——这是她说完“我知道”以后，第一次真的松开一样可以被别人拿去检查的东西。
Roman站在被允许的距离外，目光沉，肩线绷紧。Adrian能感觉到那道视线像一只手，按在他的后背上。

zh.hint: Sienna在等你开条件。合作、收材料，还是先让她公开改口？

opts.t: 限时合作。只查案，不谈别的。
then: Adrian要求双方各自的法务拟一份有限合作：期限、资料、保密、怎么终止，一条一条写清楚。
我也不会对外把它说成其中任何一种。
签名的时候，Adrian的笔尖顿了一下。门外，Roman的呼吸明显沉了一拍。
opts.rthink: 他签了。限时、限范围、不谈私人——他在纸上替我划了一条线。……我该谢他吗？

opts.t: 你可以当资料来源。不必当我的盟友。
then: Adrian把副本交给独立接收人。
你可以是资料来源，不必成为我的盟友。
Sienna眼里的失落一闪就过。Roman的肩线，几乎不可察地松了一点。
opts.rthink: 他没让她站到身边。我肩膀松下来的那一下，他看见了没有？

opts.t: 先公开更正：我没同意那份婚约。
then: Sienna在独立见证线路里确认，这份婚约未获Adrian本人承认，并向主办方提交了更正。Adrian等到回执出现在屏幕上，才点了一下头。他没有因此答应她一顿饭。
那三个字从胸腔里压出来，Adrian的耳尖跟着热了一下。
opts.rthink: 他当着见证人说“我没同意”。……十年了，我第一次听见他替自己说“不”。

zh: 灯亮起来。Adrian看得见第一排的人，却看不清镜头后面有多少人，在等一句可以被剪走的话。
提词器给他的第一句是“感谢家族”。他没有照着念。
我昨天才被告知父亲是谁。我来这里，是来核验接下来会发生的事——不是假装我已经全都懂了。
第一排的Evelyn没有鼓掌。Julian抬起了眼。Adrian的手指压住讲台边缘，又慢慢松开。他没有突然学会管理一个财团，只是终于不用为了让自己站在这里显得合理，去冒充另一个人。
Roman在侧翼的安全位。耳机里，他的呼吸很稳，稳里带着一点几乎压不住的热——像看着自己的人，第一次把自己的名字完整地说出口。

zh.hint: 全场都在等你的下一句。你要把哪个问题，说给所有人听？

opts.t: 公布我能决定什么，也公布我不能决定什么。两样都给我书面说明。
then: 董事会秘书接到核验请求。Adrian一直站在台上，等到接收编号出现在屏幕上，才走下来。
opts.rthink: 他没说漂亮话，他要编号。……这比“我不会屈服”难对付一百倍。Evelyn的笔停了。

opts.t: 以我的名义宣布的那份婚约，我没有同意。
then: 闪光灯一连串炸开。主办方当场暂停了所有称谓。Adrian没有把吸引、合作，或者一起出席，改写成“同意”。

then.why: 他当众否认了婚约

opts.rthink: 他当着两百个人说了“没有同意”。我站在侧翼，手心全是汗。……不是因为危险。

opts.t: 两份邀请都用了我的名字，只有一份通过核验。请解释另一份。
then: 主厅经理把名单的版本记录交给了法律席。舞台上一句具体的要求，比一句响亮的“我不会屈服”，更难被掌声盖过去。
opts.rthink: 他把那道错误的门摆到了台面上。动手的人现在知道，他们被看见了。……我得站得再近一点。

zh: 第一秒，玻璃落地。Adrian的身体比意识先动——他没喊，只是肩背一下绷紧。
第二秒，他听见右边有人吸了一口气。

then: 第三秒，一具身体从侧面挡了上来。胸口先贴住他的后背——热度先到，然后是心跳，然后是压在发顶的呼吸，热的、湿的，带着紧张时才有的急促。黑暗里，两个人的轮廓几乎嵌在一起。
else: 第三秒，耳机里Roman的声音一下子近了：“别动。我在过来。”他今晚本不该在场，可他还是在。

zh: 同一秒，有一只手擦过他的袖口——指腹的温度很短，带着一点凉，和金属边缘的硬。那一下像电流，从袖口一路麻到肩胛。
第四秒，一句话贴着耳廓进来，气息喷在皮肤上：
第五秒，耳机要求他沿已确认的出口移动。第六秒，有人在叫经理。

then: Roman没有立刻松开。又停了半秒，才把距离拉回安全范围。Adrian的后背上全是他留下的热，袖口却还残着陌生人碰过的凉。两种感觉叠在同一具身体上，让他一时很难站稳。
else: 值班员挤过人群，先问他有没有受伤。

zh: “碰过我”三个字说出口，他的耳尖红了。Roman的目光沉了一瞬，像把这句话里的意思，连同危险一起吞了下去。

zh.title: 袖口里多了一样东西
zh.txt: 一枚很薄的储存片，卡在你的右袖口里。送它的人没有留下名字。

zh: 备用灯没有让模糊的记忆变成高清。可袖口被碰过的那个位置，还留着一点热。

zh.title: 听到 · 感觉到 · 记录到
zh.hint: 值班员递来记录板：只写你真的知道的事。没有证据的，不能写成证据。

win.title: 记录 {pct}% 可核验
win.txt: 你没有替任何人编造证词。

win: 值班员把记录板翻过来签字，看他的眼神变了一点。
lose: 记录板上有一行被值班员划掉了：没有证据的猜测，不能进亲历栏。
Adrian盯着那道横线，耳根发烫。今晚，他最不能做的，就是变成另一个替别人编故事的人。
skip: Adrian只在亲历栏写了一行：有人碰过我的右袖。其余空着。

opts.t: 独立接收。回执留在我手机上。
then: Adrian看着编号贴上封口，逐字核对接收时间。回执存进了他自己的手机。
opts.rthink: 他谁都没交。连我也没有。……这是对的。我教过他的。

opts.t: Roman，你来看外部编码。东西由独立人员保管。
then: 在见证下，Roman俯身看那枚储存片的外部编码。看到第三行，他的呼吸停了一下。
那就写明是什么时候。别只是把屏幕挪开。
Roman拿起笔。这是今晚第一次，记录逼近了他自己的过去。握笔的手指因为用力，微微发白。
opts.rthink: 我认得这个格式。十年前，我在一间没有窗的屋子里见过它。……他让我写下来。我写了。

opts.t: Sienna协助提交。她不认证，只签提交说明。
then: Sienna签了提交说明，写明自己不是送片的人。她写字很快，最后一笔顿了一下。
Adrian看她写完，把回执拍了下来。
opts.rthink: 他把东西交给了她的人。程序上没错。……我站在三步外，什么都没说。

zh: 会客室墙角堆着折叠椅，空气里有清洁液的味道。Adrian坐下，肩胛骨抵着硬邦邦的椅背，逼自己别往前倾。
Roman站在桌子另一侧。这个距离，刚好让Adrian看清他领口的起伏、绷紧的下颌，和放在桌沿、因为用力而发白的手指。
那个格式。不是整份文件。
Roman把他能确认的年份写了出来：十年前。三年前那次，是他回到保护岗位的安排——不能拿来盖住这一个答案。他报年份时声音很稳，喉结却滚了两下。
Adrian盯着那一点，想起自己的嘴唇碰过那里——在飞机上，在书房，在所有差一点失控的夜里。记忆里的触感，比现在的质问更早一步爬上舌根。
你一直在回答你更愿意回答的那个问题。
承认的那一声很短。他早就知道这个人有所隐瞒，亲眼看他承认，还是会疼。也还是会想绕过桌子，去碰一碰那截紧绷的下颌——用体温确认这个人还在，而不是用问题把他推远。
别让认识你这件事，变成我没能保护好自己。
Roman抬起头，没有走近。肩线绷紧，呼吸沉。

zh.hint: 年份写在纸上。他承认了，可还有一半没说。关系和工作，你要怎么分开处理？

opts.t: 明天给我书面说明。今晚，继续工作。
then: Adrian写下明天的接收时间，要Roman列清楚：事实、缺失的部分、无法核验的部分。
Roman继续承担已授权的工作。私人的那半步，没有被奖励回来。可两个人之间的空气，还热着。
opts.rthink: 他给了我一个期限，而不是一扇关上的门。……明天中午之前，我得决定说到哪一页。

opts.t: 撤销你的贴身授权。走正式交接。
then: Roman按值班流程，一件一件移交器材和权限。
这不是判决。是对访问权限的限制。
新的安全员出现在门口时，Roman的目光在Adrian脸上停了两秒，才移开。那两秒里，想要和忍着缠在一起，几乎要满出来。
opts.rthink: 他说“不是判决”。我知道。可我交出去的耳机，是十年来唯一能听见他呼吸的东西。

opts.t: 从现在起，叫我Vale先生。只走正式渠道。
then: 从现在起，叫我Vale先生。只走正式渠道。
听见那个称呼，Adrian才知道，自己刚才确实关掉了一样东西。胸口空得发疼。
opts.rthink: Vale先生。……我练过这三个字。三年里每天都练。真说出口，比我想的难。

opts.t: 我想抱一下。答案我也照样要。
then: 我想抱一下。答案，我也照样要。
Roman先确认了一遍，才靠近。脚步很稳，呼吸却已经乱了一拍。手臂环上来的力道大得几乎发疼，却留出了一道随时能退出去的空隙。
Adrian的额头碰到他的肩。衣料底下的体温很真实，胸膛贴着胸膛，两颗心跳乱成一片。贴得这么近，身体的反应谁也藏不住——两个人都察觉了，谁也没有往下伸手。
Roman的手落在他背上，掌心张开，却没有再往下滑。像用尽全力，把所有想要都按在“拥抱”这两个字里。
（同样气声）我知道。别再贴近了。我会停不住。
Adrian先松开。分开时，两个人都多停了一秒，才把呼吸收回去。Roman的耳尖红了，Adrian的也是。纸上的年份还躺在桌上，像一道没被体温融化的线。
opts.rthink: 他说“答案照样要”。所以这个拥抱不是原谅，是利息。……我抱得太紧了。他没推开。

zh: 唱片店的卷帘门落了一半，里面的灯偏黄，雨从卷帘边缘滴下来。地址是真的，不代表店里安全——接收人员先确认了会面区域，Adrian才弯腰钻进去。
Marcus不在。椅子上放着一张接收单，一个保护袋里露出一角旧照片。

zh.title: 一张你没见过的照片
zh.txt: 便利店门口。年轻的Roman右臂上有伤，你站在画面边缘。拍摄者不明。

zh: 我记得那个袋子。不记得这个角度。

then: Roman只看共享副本，没伸手去碰原件。

zh: Adrian看着照片里的少年。十年不是一段把他剪成如今这个男人的蒙太奇——中间有太多天，Adrian一天也没见过。
可他还是能从成年Roman的肩背、呼吸和克制里，认出那个差一点吻他的人。

opts.t: 原件留着。我要知道是谁拍的。
then: Adrian要求提供者说明取得方式。他把生活的记忆写在私人页，把来源问题写在取证页，两页分开。
opts.rthink: 他把回忆和证据分成两页写。……他比我会保护自己。

opts.t: Roman，只说你确实记得的部分。
then: 只讲你记得的。别替我把这一幕补完。
那天我送你回家。右臂的伤已经处理过了。后面的时间，不在照片里。
听见“送你回家”，Adrian的喉咙动了一下。
Roman没有说自己一直都做得很好。照片里的伤，没给后来的离开赢回原谅。可他的目光落在Adrian脸上时，还带着一点几乎压不住的热。
opts.rthink: “你做得很好。”……十年里我对自己说过一万句话，没有一句是这个。

opts.t: 今天不看了。先问Marcus。
then: Adrian把保护袋交给保管人员，给Marcus发了一条消息。对方没有马上回。

then.why: 他绕过了Roman，直接去问Marcus

opts.rthink: 他去问Marcus，不问我。……我活该。

zh: 计划在接收室里定下来。Adrian要用一条经过批准的测试通知，找出泄露范围：一条不含任何真实人员位置的“设备转移”消息，经可疑的内部通道发出，目的地是一个没人会去的封闭装卸区。
我要知道是哪条通道漏的。不用把自己站进去。
通知发出去。第一分钟，什么都没有。第二分钟，路口一辆车转了向。独立人员记下它的路线；门禁系统里，多了一条外门申请——用的是和先前那张错误入场码同名的凭证。

zh.title: 有人咬钩了
zh.txt: 一辆无牌车驶向空无一人的装卸区。申请凭证，与那道“错误的门”同名。

opts.t: 保全路线，不再靠近。
then: Adrian让观察人员结束追踪，拿到影像和原始时间。完整的报告保存了下来。
opts.rthink: 他没追。……他知道对方要的是什么。

opts.t: 交给独立调查渠道继续处理。
then: 接收人登记了案件材料。几分钟后，他们提交了一张依法调取的访客证件照片。

then.title: 访客证件 · ROMAN CROSS
then.txt: 照片上是一张陌生的成年男人的脸。有人在用Roman的名字进出Vale。

then: Roman盯着那张证件，下颌的线条一点一点绷死。
opts.rthink: 有人戴着我的名字。……十年前他们就这么干过。这一次，我不会让它再落到他头上。

opts.t: 先停掉异常通道，再查历史。
then: Adrian申请暂停与证据有关的凭证权限。历史记录没有随着停用被删除——检索返回了一条旧档案关联。
opts.rthink: 他先关门，再翻旧账。……那份旧账里，有我的名字。

zh: 零点刚过，会客区只亮着桌子上方那一盏灯。Adrian把两份档案放在同一张垫纸上。

zh.title: 两份档案，同一个名字
zh.txt:
A：ROMAN CROSS — PROTECTIVE DETAIL（贴身护卫）
B：ROMAN CROSS — ASSET DISPOSAL APPROVED（资产处置·已批准）

zh: B的批准日期，是十年前Roman消失的第二天。不是七年前，不是三年前。Adrian把那个日期圈了起来。笔尖在纸上发出很轻的声音，Roman的呼吸跟着那一点声音沉了一拍。
我跟着一个不认识的人，离开了镇子。
回答之前的那一秒，比今晚任何一次断电都长。Roman的呼吸沉下去，肩线绷紧，放在桌边的手指一点点发白，像在忍着不去捏皱什么。

zh.hint: 他问你签过什么。桌上两份档案，一份写着保护，一份写着处置。你只能说你真的知道的。

opts.t: 一份隔离协议。不是这份处置授权。
then: 一份隔离协议。不是这份处置授权。
opts.rthink: 隔离协议。他连这四个字都没打算瞒我。……那他还瞒了什么？

opts.t: ……一份隔离协议。条款我现在说不全，但不是这一份。
then: ……一份隔离协议。条款我现在说不全。但不是这一份。
说不全。能说的，我明天写给你。
opts.rthink: “说不全。”他十七岁就这样：不撒谎，只少说。少说的那部分，才是我该查的。

opts.t: 我签过一份隔离协议。那天之后，我连自己的名字都不能用。
then: 我签过一份隔离协议。那天之后，我连自己的名字都不能用。
Adrian的笔停在纸上。十年里他设想过一百种理由，没有一种是“连名字都不能用”。
opts.rthink: 连名字都不能用。……所以那张证件上，才是一张陌生人的脸。

zh: 那就分开核验。两份都查。
B的批准栏里有一个缩写：R.C.。
两个字母证明不了签名是谁的，却够让Adrian想起Roman握笔的样子。
十七岁，指节上沾着一点蓝墨水，嫌他借的笔太滑，最后还是把名字写在一张再普通不过的纸上。现在，那份熟悉变得危险。
你不能替我挑，过去的哪一部分值得查。
这又是一个承诺。写下来。
Roman在自己的说明页上写了，没有签在那份还没核验的授权旁边。写字时，他的肩线因为用力微微绷紧，衬衫被拉出一道浅痕；喉结滚动，呼吸压得很低。
Adrian盯着他低垂的睫毛，忽然很清楚：自己想碰的不是档案，是这个人。想用手指确认他的脉搏，想用嘴唇堵住那些没说完的句子，想用身体把“你还在”按进彼此的皮肤里。
他没有动。只是把笔放下，指尖在桌面上停了两秒，像在忍着不要伸手。

t: roman
R.C.不是我签的。可我不能证明。……我能做的，只是今晚还站在这里，让他看着我写。

zh: 灯光只照亮桌面。第三章开始之前，Adrian得决定：谁，可以坐在他身边。
en: Before the phone can go dark, Adrian touches the screen again. The photo lights back up.
A red dot sits on Roman's chest. The shot doesn't show who's holding the gun. No timestamp.
Adrian spreads two fingers and the pixels break his shirt into blocks that prove nothing. The red stays put, same spot every time, like a mole about to burst.
He stares at it, and his palms go hot first. He's had his face against that chest. He's heard the heartbeat under that shirt, been hauled into that warmth when the plane dropped.
The red dot and the remembered heat land on top of each other, and his stomach clenches. Danger is supposed to make you calm. His body refuses before he can.
Right now I need him alive. Whatever else I want from him, I can tally later.
A soft sound outside the door. The elevator, arriving.

This morning he thought the worst thing he'd face was his boss's text: "Revisions by noon." Now he's standing in a foyer he has no memory of, carpet so thick his steps make no sound, and the little screen by the lock shows him the hallway in perfect detail.
Roman stands to the left of the elevator. Same dark shirt, same unsmoothed crease at the cuff. His shoulders fill the fabric, his chest barely moving as he breathes.
The living man has one thing the photo doesn't: breath. And a body that runs warm, that tenses, that shifts its weight a little when it's nervous.

Adrian watches that small rise and fall and suddenly hates his own eyes. They still remember that when Roman turns, his waist moves first and his shoulders follow. They remember the strip of collarbone at his open collar, how it looks paler under light.
Danger hasn't killed the pull. It's just made it harder to admit. Like a burn hidden under a sleeve: it hurts when you touch it, and you keep touching it to check it's still there.
Away from the window. Check the lock first.

Adrian looks at where he's standing. He's nowhere near the window. The order comes out too practiced, and suddenly the fear has somewhere to aim. Roman's voice comes from low in his chest. Low, steady, a little rough, like it's being held down.
Check yourself first. Where are you standing right now?
Roman looks up into the door camera. He doesn't pretend he doesn't know he's being watched. On screen his jaw is tight, and his throat moves once as he swallows.
East elevator. Solid wall on my left, service corridor on my right.
How long are you planning to stand there?
Until exits and passages are cleared.

Roman presses his earpiece and reads off the duty desk's badge number. The resonance in his chest carries down the line and hums in Adrian's ear. Adrian finds the same number on the lock screen. For the first time tonight, an answer checks out somewhere other than Roman.
Don't open the door to prove you're not scared.
Then don't stand there to prove you can protect me.
Roman doesn't answer right away. Through the peephole, the hand at his side slowly opens. His knuckles are still white from gripping too hard. The color comes back a little at a time.
Adrian watches that hand. It's held his waist, locked around his wrist, yanked him into Roman's arms when the plane dropped. The memory of it climbs his spine before the danger does.

then: At the edge of the frame, Roman's phone is lit with the photo Adrian forwarded. The red dot on his chest lines up with the body in front of the camera, still breathing.
Keep the original. Don't crop it. I've already had security pull footage for that window.
So you got it, and you still walked to the elevator?
I'm on the fallback route. What you're seeing is me waiting for the passage to clear.
He presses closer to the solid wall. The wall leaves a faint line in his shirt, and his back and shoulders only stand out more.
Roman hears "inside." He doesn't take it as forgiveness. His throat works, like he's swallowing something back.
Okay. Let's finish this step first.

then.why: He sent Roman the threat right away

then: As he says it, his left hand closes around his right wrist on its own. Outside, Roman's eyes are on the camera, steady. Steady enough that Adrian feels seen through. Not the lie. The urge to stand between the danger and the door by himself.
No. I'm asking about the part I don't know.

It comes too late. But Adrian knows he's doing the same thing. He forwards the photo to the duty desk and copies Roman. Once it's sent, his grip on his wrist lets go. His fingertips leave shallow marks.
I wanted you farther from the danger.
You can tell me to leave. Don't delete what I need to make the call.
Roman glances down at the image. On screen his jaw tightens, his shoulders lock for a second, and then he makes himself loosen.

His voice has cooled a degree. Every work instruction is still there. The personal part doesn't come back with them. Adrian stares at the screen and suddenly wants to reach straight through the door and touch the warmth that cold is sitting on.

then.why: He almost carried it alone again

then: A notice from the duty desk covers the photo: Anomalous access on an internal channel. Scope not yet confirmed.
Not a name. Not a promise that everyone in this building can be trusted. Adrian's fingers tighten on the edge of the screen, knuckles going white.
I already traced the source once. It came through an internal channel.

Adrian reads off the log number. Roman repeats it back. He doesn't tell him to undo it. He doesn't praise him for catching anyone either. On screen, Roman's breathing drops a beat, like he's pushing anger back down into his chest.
Don't widen the share. Secure that record first.
You want me to hand over my phone?
No. I want a separate, independent copy.
Adrian keeps the phone in his own palm and hits export. Finally, one thing in this building that doesn't have to go to Vale's people just because it's called Vale property.
Still, he can feel Roman's eyes through the camera on his hand. Heavy enough to drag him through the door.

then.why: The trace points inside Vale

else: Adrian scrolls down. The convenience store entrance. A plastic bag. Teenage Roman reaching toward the camera. The line on the back of the photo is still there: "He never should have come back for you."
Suddenly he doesn't want anyone to see this photo. Not because it hides some big secret. Because someone took a thing he'd kept close and used it to prove they could get into even that small place.
In the picture, Roman's shoulders haven't finished filling out, but you can already see the frame that would later fill a dress shirt.
They have that old picture of us.
Roman's face changes on screen. Briefly, but long enough for Adrian to see it: jaw locked, eyes going dark for an instant, like something hit him from the inside.
You're holding two drinks. Mine's still unopened.
Roman drops his eyes for a second. The camera catches the shadow of his lashes and the curve of his collar rising with his breath.
Keep the original for now. I'm also going to find out how they got that photo.
You don't remember what I drink, but you remember which picture?
I remember you didn't drink it. You spent that whole night waiting for me to finish talking.
Adrian closes the photo. Something knocks softly inside his chest.

The man outside doesn't give the answer he couldn't give ten years ago. He just reports his position again. Adrian watches the living body on the screen and understands it clearly: danger makes him want to touch Roman more, not run.

else.why: The photo from when they were seventeen

en.hint: At the lock screen, his hand hovers over the switch. The man outside is waiting for one sentence. Send him back, let him in, or don't hang up yet?

opts.t: Don't plan around me. Walk me through the route.
then: Adrian props his phone next to the lock screen. With both feeds lit side by side, he realizes he's been watching only Roman, not the hallway behind him.
I can't see the right side of the frame. What's there?
Service room. From your end, there's no way to confirm it's empty.
So you're not safe just because I can see you.

One word, and his urge to handle everything himself goes quiet. He has the duty desk state the verified fallback route first, then has Roman repeat the next step back. No jargon. Just where to go, when to stop, and who confirms.

Roman backs off behind the solid wall as instructed. The second that broad shape leaves the frame, Adrian's hand clenches. He almost calls him back. Not out of fear. It's that in the one second the body is off-screen, there's a hole in his chest.
Inside the safe zone. Didn't enter the service room.
I'm in the safe zone. Adrian, I'm still here.

The words go straight from the earpiece into his ear, low and steady, with the hum of Roman's chest behind them. Adrian holds the talk button and closes his eyes and lets them stay in his ear half a second longer. He doesn't open the door. For the first time, he doesn't treat the closed door as proof that he can't do anything.
opts.rthink: He asked about the route, not me. ...That's better. He's finally stopped standing in the doorway for me.

opts.t: Don't come in tonight. Get your relief to the duty desk.
then: Is that not coming into this apartment tonight, or not running your personal security anymore?
The first one. The second, we discuss tomorrow. In writing.
The question is so precise it makes it harder for Adrian to stay angry. Like even a refusal only counts if Roman catches it gracefully.
You don't have to act like you understand me this well.
Roman turns his head and tells the relief to report to the duty desk and send over a badge number. Adrian's phone gets no long explanation.

Just the handoff location, the confirmation time, the next security notice. Those few lines are colder than any "I'm worried about you," and they make him want to reach out and touch the man who sent them.
He regrets it as soon as it's out. Roman doesn't use it as a reason to walk back to the door.
You told me not to come in tonight. I'm doing what you said.

The elevator doors open again. The steel slides shut over that familiar shoulder a little at a time. The shirt catches the light once more, then it's gone. He wanted distance. Now that he has it, his body isn't happy. Like someone pulled something warm out of his hand, leaving only empty, and an itch.
He presses the phone to the cold door and leaves it there a long time before he pulls it back. The cold of the door doesn't touch the heat in his fingertips.
opts.rthink: He said "tonight." Not "from now on." ...I can hear the difference. I'm right downstairs. I'm not going anywhere.

opts.t: Come in after the passage is cleared. Don't touch me tonight.
then: Passage confirmation pops up on the lock screen. Adrian double-checks with the duty desk before he slides the chain.

As the chain slides free, cool night air comes in first, then Roman's scent right behind it. Gun oil, aftershave, a little sweat from nerves. Adrian breathes in before he can stop himself. His chest goes tight.

Roman is standing farther back than he expected, his dress shoes stopped just outside the edge of the foyer rug. There's a crease in his collar where the earpiece wire rubbed. The shadow along his jaw sits low. The voice that was so calm in his ear has a chest behind it at this distance.
I didn't let you in to stand guard.
You didn't let me in to touch you either.
Up close, Roman is always harder to deal with than on a screen. Broader through the back, heavier breathing, more weight in his eyes. Adrian steps back.
Roman waits until he's cleared a path before he comes in. His shoulder brushes Adrian's on the way past. When the fabric touches, they both go rigid. Neither one looks back.
Roman goes to the far side of the kitchen island. No reaching. No blocking the exit. But the space they've deliberately left between them is already hot, like a wire burning in the middle.
opts.rthink: "Don't touch me." He was looking at my hands when he said it. ...I'll keep my hands where he can see them.

opts.t: I can't put a whole sentence together right now. Don't hang up yet.
then: Adrian puts his back to the door. He's been giving orders and asking questions all night, like as long as there's one thing he's still arranging, tonight won't slide back into that night ten years ago when no one answered his texts. Now he's out of words. His chest goes tight, like someone is pressing on his breath through skin and muscle.
Don't tell me to breathe. Just don't hang up.

No "calm down." No "trust me." Just the faint rustle of fabric in his ear, and Roman confirming his fallback position with the duty desk. Adrian slides down the door to the floor. The carpet is soft. It's so soft it makes him angrier.
Roman's breath stops for a second. That second of silence on the line says more than any explanation.

Adrian wipes a hand down his face. His fingertips come away dry. He didn't cry. It doesn't help much. Once the passage clears, Roman asks if he wants the duty officer to come up first. Adrian picks the duty officer. Roman stays on the line until they arrive. Then he hangs up.
The phone is still in his hand. His palm is burning, like he just held something over the line he shouldn't have.
opts.rthink: He said "don't hang up yet." Ten years ago I hung up on him, and he still remembers. This time I'm staying on until the last second.

then: Forty minutes later the duty desk pushes an urgent notice: Confirmed presence on the east roof. Penthouse lockdown escalated. The relief is stuck at the garage security check. Protocol says the nearest licensed guard goes inside.
The doorbell doesn't ring. On the lock screen, Roman stands outside the edge of the rug, hands at his sides, waiting for him.
Adrian looks at that face for a long time. Then he hits unlock.

en: The floor-to-ceiling windows lock on their own. The heavy curtains come down one panel at a time. The room is left with the low hum of the HVAC and two people whose breathing hasn't settled.

Roman checks the last window. When he turns, the shirt pulls tight with the motion, and the lines of his back and waist are too clear in the low light. His sleeves are rolled to the elbow, the veins in his forearms moving as he works. A drop of sweat slides from his temple to his jaw and disappears into his collar.
Adrian leans against the island and watches him. The danger isn't over, but his body answers first. Not fear. The need to get a little closer. Like something under his skin gave him a small push.
Roman walks up to him and stops one step away. No closer, no farther. Just close enough for Adrian to smell him, to see the skin at his collar rise and fall with his breath.
From now on, outside communication goes over encrypted lines only. There'll be a threat dashboard on your phone.

en.title: THREAT LEVEL: HIGH
en.txt: Protection active · New: internal access logs / silent distress signal

en: Adrian doesn't look at the screen. He's looking at Roman's hand at his side. It just unclenched. The color is back in the knuckles, but it's still tight from the effort. He wants to touch that wrist. Make sure the pulse is still going.
He doesn't move. Roman catches him looking anyway. His throat moves once.
You don't have to open the door tonight. You tell me to back off, I'll back off. But know this: what I'm backing off from isn't the responsibility. It's the distance.
Adrian looks up. The one step of empty space between them is suddenly scorching.

t: roman
He watches my hands. Every time he's scared, he watches my hands, like as long as they're still moving, I'm still alive. ...So let him watch.

en: The fight comes fast. It isn't about the threat. It's about who gets to decide for whom. Roman insists he has to accept the full security plan.
Adrian won't be locked in a cage with "protection" printed on the side. Neither of them raises his voice. The air is tight enough to crack.

Roman stands on the other side of the island. At some point his top button came undone, and the line of his collarbone is sharp in the low light. The light falls along his jaw, the muscle there standing out where he's clenching it. The veins on the back of his hand run tight all the way up his forearm.

Adrian stares at that spot. The anger and the urge to touch him are knotted together and won't come apart. The island is the only barrier left. Without it, he isn't sure he wouldn't walk around it and use his hands instead of his next question.
You disappear for ten years. Now you show up giving me orders.
I give orders because I don't have any other way to make sure you stay alive.
Then what did you promise? Ten years ago, what did you promise?
Roman's breathing drops a beat. His jaw locks, his shoulders tip forward slightly, like his body went on guard before his mouth did.

en.hint: He's waiting for you to answer "what did you promise ten years ago." You can keep pushing, you can tell the truth, or you can say nothing at all.

opts.t: Answer me. One at a time. Don't hide behind "protection."
then: Adrian throws the questions one after another and doesn't give Roman a chance to rename the past as "protection."
Where did you go that night? Who told you to leave? Before you left, did you even think about calling me?
Roman's answers keep getting shorter. His eyes keep getting darker. When the fight finally stops, the air between them is cold enough to burn. Not the temperature. Everything they're holding down.
opts.rthink: Every question hits the same place. The shorter I answer, the more he knows I'm dodging. ...He's always known.

opts.t: ...I'm scared. Scared you'll disappear again.
then: I'm scared. Scared you'll disappear again. Scared I'll be standing in another night where nobody answers.
Then he takes half a step forward. Roman's whole body stiffens, but he doesn't back away. Adrian's forehead nearly touches his jaw. He can feel Roman's breath on his lips. Warm.
Roman's hand comes up and stops in midair. In the end it just touches the outside of Adrian's arm, barely, like it hit a live wire, and pulls back.
...Don't. If I touch you now, I won't stop.
opts.rthink: He said he's scared. In ten years I imagined him hating me, forgetting me. I never once imagined him scared. My hand stopped in midair because one more inch and I'd have no right to the word "protect."

opts.t: *He stops arguing and reaches up to undo the second button on Roman's shirt.*
then: Adrian stops arguing. He reaches up and undoes the second button on Roman's shirt. His fingertips skim the collarbone, then lower, and stop on his chest. The muscle under the skin goes tight all at once.
Roman's breathing goes heavy and rough. He catches Adrian's wrist but doesn't pull it away. Instead he presses that hand harder against his chest, right over a heart going out of its mind.

The next second, the small of his back hits the edge of the island. Roman's kiss is deep and heavy, ten years of unsaid things coming down with it. His palm is flat on Adrian's side, thumb pressing into the dip above his hip hard enough to almost leave a mark. Pressed this close, neither of them can hide a thing.
But he stops before he actually crosses the line. Forehead against Adrian's, his breathing a mess.
Not before the vote... I can't lose control.
Adrian leans in again, on purpose. Roman swears under his breath and pulls him all the way into his arms, chin resting on top of his head, and doesn't let go for a long time.
Interrupt me like that again and whatever happens is on you.

then.title: Ten Minutes at the Island
then.teaser: He said he "can't lose control," but he didn't let go. The ten minutes before the lights went out belong to the two of you.
then: The curtains are down tight, the whole city shut outside. The penthouse is left with the low drone of the air and two people breathing out of rhythm.

Roman backs him against the island. His mouth moves from Adrian's lips to his jaw, then to the pulse at the side of his neck, the one beating fastest. Every touch is slow, like he's checking that Adrian is still alive.
Shirt buttons come undone one at a time. The moment a palm meets skin, they both shiver. Everything ten years stored up finds a way out in those ten minutes.
(against his ear) Say stop, and I'll stop.

The light doesn't remember much of what comes after. Only that Roman never let go of his hand, fingers laced, knuckles pressed to the cold countertop. Only that at the very end Roman buried his face in the curve of his neck and said his name, his voice so hoarse it didn't sound like his.
A long time later, Roman lifts his head and smooths Adrian's collar back into place, slowly. His thumb rests on Adrian's collarbone for a moment.
Before the vote, this is the last time.
You said that last time too.
...Last time I wasn't lying to you. This time I'm lying to myself.

opts.rthink: His fingers were shaking when he undid my button. He thinks I didn't notice. I held his hand there, and not to stop him. I didn't want him to notice I was shaking worse.

en: The fight has stopped, but the air in the penthouse doesn't cool right away. The AC holds the temperature steady, and Adrian's skin is still hot. Heat left by everything that was just said, by the places that got touched and the ones that didn't. Like it's been pressed under his skin and won't fade yet.

Roman stands on the other side of the island, top two buttons still open, sweat running down the side of his neck into his collar. He's in no hurry to fix himself up, like he's decided Adrian has a right to see this.
You always stop at the edge.
Because once I cross it, I won't give you another chance to say "don't touch me tonight."
His voice is low, a little hoarse. Adrian can hear it rumble in his chest. They hold each other's eyes for a few seconds. The air is full of unfinished things and danger nobody's spelled out.
Roman finally does the buttons back up, one at a time, slowly, like he's giving Adrian time for one last look. At the second button his fingers pause before they go on.
Go change. There's one more door to get through tonight.

en.title: Vale Welcome Reception · Tonight, 11 PM
en.txt: The board has called a last-minute reception tonight to welcome the heir. Location: the main ballroom, Vale Hotel. Your name is already on the guest list. Twice.

en: When Adrian turns away, he can feel that gaze land on the small of his back. It doesn't look away. It doesn't come any closer either. Like a knife back in its sheath, the edge still hot.
Once the lockdown is done, the penthouse goes quiet except for the low hum of the AC and two men whose breathing hasn't quite settled.

Roman finishes his last sweep of the doors and windows. His shirt has gone damp in places, sticking to his shoulders and chest. He comes over to the island and, without a word, slides a bottle of water toward Adrian. His fingers stay on it half a second too long, like he's checking whether he's still allowed this close.
Adrian takes the water. His fingertips brush Roman's knuckles. They both go still.
Your heart rate was way up back in that hallway.
Roman's Adam's apple bobs. He doesn't step back. He doesn't step closer either. The one pace of air between them runs hot.
If there's another round tonight, pick staying alive first. Right and wrong can wait.
And you? What do you pick?
You. Where I can see you.
When he's said it, his eyes drop to Adrian's mouth for a beat before he makes himself look away.

en.txt: It's not that I don't want to finish the sentence. It's that once I do, you'll know I owe you more than you think.

en.why: You. Where I can see you

en: The stylist wheels in three options: a dark suit, a white tux, and the old jacket Adrian refused to give up. A mirror takes up the whole wall, lit from all around the frame, so bright it leaves no shadows.

Roman stands three steps back, arms crossed, chin slightly down. His eyes don't stay down. They move from the back of Adrian's neck to his shoulder blades, to where the shirt pulls in at his waist, then come back up to his face with careful control. Two seconds, tops. Enough to make the tips of Adrian's ears burn.
"Enough room to move in that one?" the stylist asks.
He says it to Roman in the mirror. Roman doesn't look away. He lets out a breath, barely, like he's pushing something back down, and for a second you can see his chest rise and fall.

Adrian lifts a hand to fix his cuff, on purpose, and the shirt hem rides up half an inch, showing a strip of skin at his side. In the mirror, Roman's throat moves. His fingers tighten on his arm until the knuckles go white.
(just as low) No. So you'd better finish getting dressed.

It sounds like an order, but his voice goes rough at the end. Adrian's knees give, just slightly. In the mirror, Roman's eyes go darker for that one second. Then he wrenches them toward the door, like the job is the only thing holding him at a safe distance.

t: roman
He's doing it on purpose. He had this move down at seventeen. He'd borrow my jacket, sleeves too long, and roll them up one turn at a time right in front of me. ...I didn't hold out then, either.

en.title: Tonight's Look
en.hint: Three outfits hang in front of the mirror. Tonight there'll be cameras, board members, and a "wrong door." How do you want to walk in?

then: Adrian buttons it all the way up, decides it's too tight, and undoes the top one. In the mirror, Roman's eyes follow that small patch of bare neck, then pull back up, under control.
Adrian's hand stalls at his collar. Neither of them is allowed to turn the joke into reaching out. But the heat in the room says enough.

items.sub: Ask him to do the cuffs
then: Roman looks at him first, like he's making sure this is allowed, then comes over. He only holds the cuff, but when his fingertips graze the bone of Adrian's wrist, they both tense. His fingertips are lightly callused, and even held back, a little of his strength leaks through.
Roman's breath lands by his ear, low, almost a sigh. The cuff is done. Adrian's wrist still feels where he touched it, like an invisible stamp.
This one won't sign anything for you.
Don't let the cufflinks apologize for you, either.

The stylist checks that the pockets aren't torn and the shoes are good for walking, and brushes off the collar of the old jacket. When Adrian shrugs it on, the fabric pulls softly at his shoulders. It's his. Nobody bought it for him.
Roman looks at the old jacket, and something complicated crosses his face, like he's seeing the kid who used to wait for him outside the convenience store ten years ago.
I don't have to look like them to get to ask questions.
His voice is low, with a hurt in it he's almost managed to bury.

en.place: En route to the Vale Hotel

en: In the car, Roman sits beside him again instead of up front. A fine rain has started outside, stretching the city lights into wet streaks.

Their knees have been touching since they pulled out. He can feel the warmth through the fabric. Every turn presses their legs together a little harder. Adrian doesn't move away. Neither does Roman, as if they've both agreed this is one of the few things allowed tonight.

en.hint: His hand is right there — you can feel the heat of it through the fabric. It's dark in the back seat; no one up front can see. Your hand—

opts.t: *Cover the back of his hand, barely, and let your thumb move.*
then: After two minutes Roman's fingers shift and settle, barely there, over the back of Adrian's hand. No laced fingers — just the warmth of his palm. His thumb moves slowly along the side of Adrian's hand: once, a half-second pause, again. Like he's counting a pulse. Like he's saying: I'm here.
opts.rthink: His hand's on mine. ...I didn't pull away. I've been waiting ten years for that hand.

opts.t: *Keep your hand on your own knee. Let only your knee touch his.*
then: Roman's hand stays on his own knee, knuckles tight, not moving. Only the knee pressed against Adrian's leans in harder on every turn.
Adrian glances down at that hand, white with restraint — then reaches over and covers it himself.
opts.rthink: He's holding back. Hand clenched like that and he thinks I can't tell. ...Fine. I'll do it.

opts.t: (quietly) Cold?
then: Roman doesn't buy it. His hand settles over Adrian's, palm to the back of it, thumb moving slowly — once, a half-second pause, again.
opts.rthink: He asked if I'm cold. He knows I'm not. ...He just needed an excuse.

en: Adrian stares at the lights sliding past the window. Roman's warmth climbs from the back of his hand up his arm and into the side of his neck. He doesn't say anything. Neither does Roman. In the dark, there's just the knee and the hand, still giving off heat.
If somebody actually makes a move tonight, you're planning to step in front of me?
You ever think maybe I don't want to watch you bleed again?
I have. So I'll try to keep the blood where it belongs.
Then his thumb presses a little harder into the back of Adrian's hand. Adrian turns his head and sees the hard set of Roman's jaw, his collar rising and falling with each breath.
The thumb doesn't stop until Adrian's breathing catches. Even then, the hand stays.

en.why: In the car, the hand stayed

en: In the hotel lobby, the flowers get looked after before the people do. Water still beads on the petals, and the line outside has been waiting ten minutes. The reporters say Adrian's name like they've practiced it. On the doorman's scanner, it says PENDING.

He doesn't pull out the black card to make it go away. He asks where his two entry codes were issued. One came through the official intake channel. The other routes him through the service level, "to avoid the press."
Somebody knowing my name doesn't make their invitation real.
The doorman glances at the sign for the service level, and his face changes. Adrian has him put it in the log.
In the lobby mirror, Roman stands behind him at the agreed distance. His eyes never leave Adrian. It feels like a hand pressed to the small of his back.

en.title: Someone Left You the Wrong Door
en.txt: The second entry code sends you to the service-level loading dock. No cameras there. No reporters.

en.hint: Both invitations have your name on them. Only one is real. Which door do you take?

opts.t: Main entrance. I'll wait for the ID check.
then: Adrian stands where the cameras can see him and asks the manager what exactly they're verifying. He doesn't move until the check clears. The shutters go off like rain.

Roman stays half a step behind him, to one side. When the flashes surge, his hand lands on the small of Adrian's back. Not an arm around him. Not a show for anyone. Just his whole palm, fingers tightening slightly. Two seconds.

Once, his thumb presses right into the dip of Adrian's spine. Adrian's breath catches. He doesn't turn around, but his shoulder blades go tight. Roman seems to notice. He eases the pressure at once, but he doesn't let go.
After the hand is gone, that patch of skin stays hot. It won't cool down.
opts.rthink: His back went tight under my hand. ...I should've let go. I was two seconds late.

opts.t: Legal channel. Register properly, so nobody can fault it.
then: The legal desk confirms his temporary clearance. Sienna files the paperwork, steps back to the advisor's spot, and gives him one nod, like she saw this choice coming.
As Adrian crosses the checkpoint line, Roman's eyes follow him from the other side. Heavy, hot, plainly unhappy, and held down by force.
opts.rthink: He took the route she handed him. Procedurally, it's flawless. ...It's not the procedure I don't like.

opts.t: I'm not going in. I'll give my statement remotely.
then: Adrian stays in the outer lounge, already cleared as secure, and the legal desk sets up a remote statement. When the grand hall's feed goes live, his face fills the big screen.
(in his earpiece, low) I've got eyes on you.
The voice is so low it's rough, like it was said right against his ear.
opts.rthink: If he stays out, I don't have to find the one with the knife among two hundred people. ...Did he pick this for me? I don't dare ask.

en: The table in the intake room is too narrow for a nice dinner. It's wide enough for three ugly documents.

Sienna turns to page three. Guarantees. Linked votes. The engagement, written up as a note on "stable relations between the families." A chip of her nude polish has flaked off one nail. She probably hasn't noticed.
The papers can't prove the engagement is valid. They do explain why someone would rather it looked that way.
This is what my side was hoping to get out of it.
You're not going to open with how bad it'll be for everyone else?

Adrian reads on. Employees, pensions, financing obligations, all further down. Sienna hands a copy to the intake clerk. Since she said "I know," it's the first time she's actually let go of something someone else can check.
Roman stands at the permitted distance, eyes heavy, shoulders tight. Adrian can feel that look like a hand on his back.

en.why: Sienna put her own stake on the table first

en.hint: Sienna's waiting for your terms. Work with her, take the documents, or make her retract in public first?

opts.t: Limited partnership. The case, nothing else.
then: Adrian has both sides' lawyers draft a limited agreement: term, materials, confidentiality, termination. Every clause spelled out.
And I won't tell anyone it's either.
When he signs, Adrian's pen hesitates. Outside the door, Roman's breathing drops a beat.
opts.rthink: He signed. Time limit, scope limit, nothing personal. He drew a line on paper for me. ...Should I thank him?

opts.t: You can be a source. You don't have to be my ally.
then: Adrian hands the copy to the independent intake officer.
You can be a source. You don't need to be my ally.
Disappointment crosses Sienna's eyes and is gone. Roman's shoulders loosen, barely.
opts.rthink: He didn't let her stand next to him. When my shoulders dropped, did he see?

opts.t: Public correction first: I never agreed to that engagement.
then: On the independent witness line, Sienna confirms that Adrian never acknowledged the engagement, and files a correction with the organizers. Adrian waits for the receipt to show on screen before he nods. It doesn't buy her a dinner.
(in his earpiece, barely audible) Good work.
The two words come up from deep in Roman's chest. The tips of Adrian's ears go warm.
opts.rthink: He said "I never agreed" in front of a witness. ...Ten years, and it's the first time I've heard him say no for himself.

en: The lights come up. Adrian can see the front row. He can't see how many people are behind the cameras, waiting for one line they can clip.
The teleprompter's first line is "Thank you to the family." He doesn't read it.
I found out who my father was yesterday. I'm here to verify what happens next. Not to pretend I already understand all of it.

In the front row, Evelyn doesn't clap. Julian looks up. Adrian's fingers press the edge of the podium, then slowly let go. He hasn't suddenly learned how to run a conglomerate. He just doesn't have to pretend to be someone else to justify standing here.

Roman holds his secure position in the wings. In the earpiece, his breathing is steady, with a heat under it he can barely hold down. Like watching his own person say his own name in full for the first time.

en.hint: The whole room is waiting for your next line. Which question do you put in front of everyone?

opts.t: Publish what I can decide, and what I can't. Both, in writing.
then: The board secretary receives the verification request. Adrian stays at the podium until the intake number appears on screen. Then he steps down.
opts.rthink: No pretty speech. He asked for a reference number. ...That's a hundred times harder to deal with than "I won't back down." Evelyn's pen stopped.

opts.t: The engagement announced in my name. I never agreed to it.
then: The flashes go off in a string. The organizers suspend every title on the spot. Adrian doesn't let attraction, cooperation, or showing up together get rewritten as consent.

then.why: He denied the engagement in public

opts.rthink: He said "I never agreed" in front of two hundred people. I'm in the wings with sweat in my palms. ...It isn't the danger.

opts.t: Two invitations used my name. Only one passed verification. Explain the other one.
then: The grand hall manager hands the guest list's version history to the legal desk. A specific demand from the stage is harder to drown in applause than a loud "I won't back down."
opts.rthink: He put the wrong door on the table. Whoever did it knows now they've been seen. ...I need to stand closer.

en.title: Blackout · 7 seconds
en.txt: Every light in the grand hall goes out at once.

en: One second: glass hits the floor. Adrian's body moves before his mind does. He doesn't shout. His shoulders and back just lock.
Two seconds: someone to his right draws a breath.

then: Three seconds: a body cuts in from the side and covers him. A chest against his back. The heat comes first, then the heartbeat, then breath against the top of his head, hot and damp and fast the way it only gets under pressure. In the dark, their outlines almost fit into one.
else: Three seconds: Roman's voice is suddenly close in the earpiece. "Don't move. I'm coming." He wasn't supposed to be here tonight. He's here anyway.

en: In the same second, a hand brushes his cuff. A fingertip, there and gone, a little cool, and the hard edge of metal. It runs through him like current, from his cuff to his shoulder blade.
Four seconds: words right against his ear, breath on his skin:
Five seconds: the earpiece tells him to move toward the cleared exit. Six seconds: someone is calling for the manager.
Seven seconds: the emergency lights come on.

then: Roman doesn't let go right away. Half a second more, then he steps back to a safe distance. Adrian's back is covered in the heat he left. His cuff still holds the cool of a stranger's touch. Both at once, in the same body. For a moment it's hard to stand straight.
else: A duty officer pushes through the crowd and asks first whether he's hurt.

en: The moment "touched me" is out, the tips of his ears go red. Roman's eyes darken for an instant, like he's swallowing what that means along with the danger.

en.title: Something in Your Cuff
en.txt: A thin memory chip, tucked into your right cuff. Whoever left it didn't leave a name.

en: The emergency lights don't sharpen a blurred memory. But the spot on his cuff where he was touched is still a little warm.

en.title: Heard · Felt · Recorded
en.hint: The duty officer hands you a clipboard. Write only what you actually know. Nothing without evidence goes down as evidence.

qs.q: The sound of glass hitting the floor

opts: Heard it myself. Record it word for word.

win.title: Record {pct}% Verifiable
win.txt: You didn't make up testimony for anyone.

win: The duty officer flips the clipboard around to sign. The way he looks at Adrian shifts, just slightly.
I only wrote what I actually know.
lose: The duty officer strikes out one line on the clipboard. A guess with no evidence doesn't go in the witnessed column.
Adrian stares at the line through it, his ears burning. Tonight, the last thing he can afford is to become one more person making up stories about other people.
skip: Adrian writes one line in the witnessed column: Someone touched my right sleeve. He leaves the rest blank.

en.hint: Who holds on to the chip?

opts.t: Independent intake. The receipt stays on my phone.
then: Adrian watches the number go on the seal and checks the intake time character by character. The receipt goes on his own phone.
opts.rthink: He didn't hand it to anyone. Not even me. ...That's right. I taught him that.

opts.t: Roman, you read the outer code. An independent officer keeps the chip.
then: With a witness present, Roman leans over to read the chip's outer code. At the third line, his breath stops.
Then write down when. Don't just turn the screen away.
Roman picks up the pen. For the first time tonight, the record is closing in on his own past. His fingers go pale around the pen.
opts.rthink: I know this format. Ten years ago, I saw it in a room with no windows. ...He made me write it down. I did.

opts.t: Sienna helps file it. She doesn't certify anything, just signs the filing note.
then: Sienna signs the filing note and states that she's not the one who passed the chip. She writes fast. On the last stroke, her pen pauses.
Adrian watches her finish and takes a photo of the receipt.
opts.rthink: He handed it to her people. Procedurally, nothing wrong with that. ...I stood three steps away and said nothing.

en: Folding chairs are stacked in the corner of the lounge. The air smells like cleaning fluid. Adrian sits, shoulder blades against the hard chair back, and makes himself not lean forward.
Roman stands on the other side of the table. From here Adrian can see everything: the rise and fall at his collar, the locked jaw, the fingers on the table's edge, white from pressing down.
The format. Not the whole file.

Roman writes down the one year he can confirm: ten years ago. Three years ago was his reassignment back to protection — it doesn't get to cover for this answer. His voice is steady when he says the year. His throat works twice anyway.
Adrian watches that spot and remembers his mouth there — on the plane, in the study, on every night that almost got away from them. The memory of it reaches his tongue before the next question does.
You keep answering the question you'd rather answer.

The admission is short. He's known for a while that this man was holding something back. Watching him admit it still hurts. He still wants to come around the table and touch that tight jaw — to check by touch that he's still here, instead of pushing him away with questions.
Don't make knowing you the reason I didn't protect myself.
Roman looks up. He doesn't come closer. His shoulders are tight, his breathing heavy.

en.hint: The year is on paper. He admitted it, but half of it is still unsaid. How do you keep the relationship and the work apart?

opts.t: Give me a written statement tomorrow. Tonight, we keep working.
then: Adrian writes down tomorrow's intake time and tells Roman to lay it out: the facts, what's missing, what can't be verified.
Roman keeps doing the work he's cleared for. The half step he took on the personal side doesn't get handed back to him. The air between them is still warm.
opts.rthink: He gave me a deadline, not a closed door. ...By noon tomorrow, I have to decide how many pages I tell him.

opts.t: I'm pulling your close-protection clearance. We do a formal handover.
then: Roman follows shift protocol and hands over his gear and access, one item at a time.
This isn't a verdict. It's a limit on access.

When the new officer shows up at the door, Roman's eyes stay on Adrian's face for two seconds before they move. In those two seconds, wanting and holding back are knotted so tight they almost spill over.
opts.rthink: He said "not a verdict." I know. But the earpiece I just handed over was the only thing in ten years that let me hear him breathe.

opts.t: From now on, it's Mr. Vale. Official channels only.
then: From now on, it's Mr. Vale. Official channels only.
Hearing the name, Adrian knows he really did just shut something off. His chest goes hollow, and it aches.
opts.rthink: Mr. Vale. ...I practiced those words. Every day for three years. Saying them for real was harder than I thought.

opts.t: I want a hug. I still want the answers.
then: I want a hug. And I still want the answers.
Roman checks once before he moves in. His steps are steady. His breathing already isn't. His arms close around him hard enough to almost hurt, but they leave a gap he could step out of any time.

Adrian's forehead meets his shoulder. The heat under the fabric is real. Chest to chest, two heartbeats lose their rhythm together. This close, neither of them can hide what his body is doing — they both notice, and neither of them lets a hand drift lower.
Roman's hand lands on his back, palm open, and goes no further. Like he's using everything he has to keep all that want inside the word "hug."
(just as quiet) I know. Don't come any closer. I won't be able to stop.

Adrian lets go first. When they separate, they both stay one second longer before they get their breathing back. The tips of Roman's ears are red. So are Adrian's. The year is still on the paper on the table, a line body heat didn't melt.
opts.rthink: He said "I still want the answers." So the hug isn't forgiveness. It's interest. ...I held on too tight. He didn't push me away.

en: The record store's roll-down gate is halfway shut. The light inside is yellow. Rain drips off the gate's edge. A real address doesn't mean a safe store — the intake team clears the meeting area first, and only then does Adrian duck under.
Marcus isn't there. On a chair: an intake form, and an evidence sleeve with the corner of an old photo showing.

en.title: A Photo You've Never Seen
en.txt: Outside a convenience store. Young Roman, his right arm hurt. You're at the edge of the frame. Photographer unknown.

en: I remember that bag. I don't remember this angle.

then: Roman looks only at the shared copy. He doesn't reach for the original.

en: Adrian looks at the kid in the photo. Ten years isn't a montage that cuts him into the man he is now — there are too many days in between, and Adrian didn't see a single one.
Still, in grown Roman's shoulders, his breathing, his restraint, he can find the boy who almost kissed him.

en.hint: The photo's in your hands. Next —

opts.t: The original stays here. I want to know who took it.
then: Adrian asks the source to explain how they got it. He puts what he remembers on a personal page and the sourcing questions on an evidence page. Two pages, kept apart.
opts.rthink: He put memory and evidence on separate pages. ...He's better at protecting himself than I am.

opts.t: Roman. Only what you actually remember.
then: Just what you remember. Don't fill in the rest of the scene for me.
That day I walked you home. The arm had already been taken care of. Whatever came after isn't in the photo.
At "walked you home," Adrian's throat moves.
Roman doesn't say he always did right. The injury in the photo doesn't buy forgiveness for leaving later. But when his eyes land on Adrian's face, there's a heat in them he can barely keep down.
opts.rthink: "You did right." ...I've told myself ten thousand things in ten years. That was never one of them.

opts.t: I'm done looking tonight. Marcus first.
then: Adrian hands the evidence sleeve to the custodian and sends Marcus a message. No answer right away.

then.why: He went around Roman, straight to Marcus

opts.rthink: He asked Marcus. Not me. ...I earned that.

en: The plan gets settled in the intake room. Adrian will use an approved test notice to map the leak: an "equipment transfer" message with no real person's location in it, sent through the suspect internal channel, pointing at a closed loading dock nobody will be at.
I want to know which channel is leaking. I don't need to stand in it to find out.

The notice goes out. First minute, nothing. Second minute, a car at the intersection changes direction. The independent team logs its route. In the access system, a new exterior-door request appears — under the same credential name as that bad entry code from before.

en.title: Someone Took the Bait
en.txt: An unplated car heading for an empty loading dock. The request credential has the same name as the "wrong door."

opts.t: Preserve the route. Nobody gets closer.
then: Adrian has the spotters end the tail and pull the footage and raw timestamps. The full report is saved.
opts.rthink: He didn't chase. ...He knows what they want.

opts.t: Hand it to the independent investigation channel.
then: The intake officer logs the case material. A few minutes later, they submit a lawfully obtained photo of a visitor badge.

then.title: Visitor Badge · ROMAN CROSS
then.txt: The photo shows a grown man's face. A stranger. Someone is using Roman's name to get in and out of Vale.

then: Roman stares at the badge. His jaw locks, one notch at a time.
opts.rthink: Someone's wearing my name. ...They did this ten years ago. This time I won't let it come down on him.

opts.t: Shut the bad channel first. History after.
then: Adrian requests a freeze on the credentials tied to the evidence. Freezing them doesn't erase the history — the search comes back with a link to an old file.
opts.rthink: He shuts the door first, then goes through the old books. ...My name is in those books.

en: Just past midnight. In the lounge, the only light is the one over the table. Adrian lays the two files on the same sheet of blotter paper.

en.title: Two Files, One Name
en.txt:
A: ROMAN CROSS — PROTECTIVE DETAIL (close protection)
B: ROMAN CROSS — ASSET DISPOSAL APPROVED (asset disposal · approved)

en: B's approval date is the day after Roman disappeared, ten years ago. Not seven years ago. Not three. Adrian circles the date. The pen makes a faint sound on the paper, and Roman's breathing drops with it.
I left town with someone I didn't know.

The second before he answers is longer than any blackout tonight. Roman's breathing goes deep, his shoulders tighten, and the fingers on the table's edge whiten bit by bit, like he's trying not to crush something.

en.hint: He's asking what you signed. Two files on the table — one says protection, one says disposal. Say only what you actually know.

opts.t: An isolation agreement. Not this disposal order.
then: An isolation agreement. Not this disposal order.
opts.rthink: An isolation agreement. He didn't even try to hide those words. ...So what is he hiding?

opts.t: ...An isolation agreement. I can't give you all the terms right now. But not this one.
then: ...An isolation agreement. I can't give you all the terms right now. But not this one.
Can't. What I can, I'll put in writing tomorrow.
opts.rthink: "Can't give you all of it." Same as at seventeen: he doesn't lie, he leaves things out. The part he leaves out is what I need to check.

opts.t: I signed an isolation agreement. After that day I couldn't even use my own name.
then: I signed an isolation agreement. After that day I couldn't even use my own name.
Adrian's pen stops on the paper. In ten years he imagined a hundred reasons. Not one of them was 'couldn't even use my own name.'
opts.rthink: Couldn't use his own name. ...So that's why the ID card has a stranger's face.

en: Then we verify them separately. Both of them.
In B's approval box, initials: R.C. Two letters can't prove whose signature it is.
They're enough to make Adrian remember how Roman held a pen.

Seventeen, a smudge of blue ink on his knuckles, complaining the pen Adrian lent him was too slippery, then signing his name on the most ordinary scrap of paper anyway. Now that familiarity is dangerous.
You don't get to pick which part of the past is worth checking for me.
That's another promise. Write it down.

Roman writes it on his own statement page, not next to the unverified authorization. As he writes, the effort pulls his shoulders tight and draws a faint crease across his shirt. His throat moves. He keeps his breathing low.

Adrian watches his lowered lashes and suddenly knows exactly what he wants to touch, and it isn't the file. It's him. He wants his fingers on that pulse. He wants his mouth on every sentence Roman hasn't finished. He wants to press "you're still here" into both their skin.
He doesn't move. He just sets the pen down. His fingertips rest on the table for two seconds, like he's holding himself back from reaching out.

t: roman
I didn't sign R.C. But I can't prove it. ...All I can do is still be standing here tonight, and let him watch me write.

en: The light only reaches the table. Before Chapter 3 begins, Adrian has to decide who gets to sit beside him.
ja: Before the phone can go dark, Adrian touches the screen again. The photo lights back up.
A red dot sits on Roman's chest. The shot doesn't show who's holding the gun. No timestamp.
Adrian spreads two fingers and the pixels break his shirt into blocks that prove nothing. The red stays put, same spot every time, like a mole about to burst.
He stares at it, and his palms go hot first. He's had his face against that chest. He's heard the heartbeat under that shirt, been hauled into that warmth when the plane dropped.
The red dot and the remembered heat land on top of each other, and his stomach clenches. Danger is supposed to make you calm. His body refuses before he can.
Right now I need him alive. Whatever else I want from him, I can tally later.
A soft sound outside the door. The elevator, arriving.

This morning he thought the worst thing he'd face was his boss's text: "Revisions by noon." Now he's standing in a foyer he has no memory of, carpet so thick his steps make no sound, and the little screen by the lock shows him the hallway in perfect detail.
Roman stands to the left of the elevator. Same dark shirt, same unsmoothed crease at the cuff. His shoulders fill the fabric, his chest barely moving as he breathes.
The living man has one thing the photo doesn't: breath. And a body that runs warm, that tenses, that shifts its weight a little when it's nervous.

Adrian watches that small rise and fall and suddenly hates his own eyes. They still remember that when Roman turns, his waist moves first and his shoulders follow. They remember the strip of collarbone at his open collar, how it looks paler under light.
Danger hasn't killed the pull. It's just made it harder to admit. Like a burn hidden under a sleeve: it hurts when you touch it, and you keep touching it to check it's still there.
Away from the window. Check the lock first.

Adrian looks at where he's standing. He's nowhere near the window. The order comes out too practiced, and suddenly the fear has somewhere to aim. Roman's voice comes from low in his chest. Low, steady, a little rough, like it's being held down.
Check yourself first. Where are you standing right now?
Roman looks up into the door camera. He doesn't pretend he doesn't know he's being watched. On screen his jaw is tight, and his throat moves once as he swallows.
East elevator. Solid wall on my left, service corridor on my right.
How long are you planning to stand there?
Until exits and passages are cleared.

Roman presses his earpiece and reads off the duty desk's badge number. The resonance in his chest carries down the line and hums in Adrian's ear. Adrian finds the same number on the lock screen. For the first time tonight, an answer checks out somewhere other than Roman.
Don't open the door to prove you're not scared.
Then don't stand there to prove you can protect me.
Roman doesn't answer right away. Through the peephole, the hand at his side slowly opens. His knuckles are still white from gripping too hard. The color comes back a little at a time.
Adrian watches that hand. It's held his waist, locked around his wrist, yanked him into Roman's arms when the plane dropped. The memory of it climbs his spine before the danger does.

then: At the edge of the frame, Roman's phone is lit with the photo Adrian forwarded. The red dot on his chest lines up with the body in front of the camera, still breathing.
Keep the original. Don't crop it. I've already had security pull footage for that window.
So you got it, and you still walked to the elevator?
I'm on the fallback route. What you're seeing is me waiting for the passage to clear.
He presses closer to the solid wall. The wall leaves a faint line in his shirt, and his back and shoulders only stand out more.
Roman hears "inside." He doesn't take it as forgiveness. His throat works, like he's swallowing something back.
Okay. Let's finish this step first.

then.why: He sent Roman the threat right away

then: As he says it, his left hand closes around his right wrist on its own. Outside, Roman's eyes are on the camera, steady. Steady enough that Adrian feels seen through. Not the lie. The urge to stand between the danger and the door by himself.
No. I'm asking about the part I don't know.

It comes too late. But Adrian knows he's doing the same thing. He forwards the photo to the duty desk and copies Roman. Once it's sent, his grip on his wrist lets go. His fingertips leave shallow marks.
I wanted you farther from the danger.
You can tell me to leave. Don't delete what I need to make the call.
Roman glances down at the image. On screen his jaw tightens, his shoulders lock for a second, and then he makes himself loosen.

His voice has cooled a degree. Every work instruction is still there. The personal part doesn't come back with them. Adrian stares at the screen and suddenly wants to reach straight through the door and touch the warmth that cold is sitting on.

then.why: He almost carried it alone again

then: A notice from the duty desk covers the photo: Anomalous access on an internal channel. Scope not yet confirmed.
Not a name. Not a promise that everyone in this building can be trusted. Adrian's fingers tighten on the edge of the screen, knuckles going white.
I already traced the source once. It came through an internal channel.

Adrian reads off the log number. Roman repeats it back. He doesn't tell him to undo it. He doesn't praise him for catching anyone either. On screen, Roman's breathing drops a beat, like he's pushing anger back down into his chest.
Don't widen the share. Secure that record first.
You want me to hand over my phone?
No. I want a separate, independent copy.
Adrian keeps the phone in his own palm and hits export. Finally, one thing in this building that doesn't have to go to Vale's people just because it's called Vale property.
Still, he can feel Roman's eyes through the camera on his hand. Heavy enough to drag him through the door.

then.why: The trace points inside Vale

else: Adrian scrolls down. The convenience store entrance. A plastic bag. Teenage Roman reaching toward the camera. The line on the back of the photo is still there: "He never should have come back for you."
Suddenly he doesn't want anyone to see this photo. Not because it hides some big secret. Because someone took a thing he'd kept close and used it to prove they could get into even that small place.
In the picture, Roman's shoulders haven't finished filling out, but you can already see the frame that would later fill a dress shirt.
They have that old picture of us.
Roman's face changes on screen. Briefly, but long enough for Adrian to see it: jaw locked, eyes going dark for an instant, like something hit him from the inside.
You're holding two drinks. Mine's still unopened.
Roman drops his eyes for a second. The camera catches the shadow of his lashes and the curve of his collar rising with his breath.
Keep the original for now. I'm also going to find out how they got that photo.
You don't remember what I drink, but you remember which picture?
I remember you didn't drink it. You spent that whole night waiting for me to finish talking.
Adrian closes the photo. Something knocks softly inside his chest.

The man outside doesn't give the answer he couldn't give ten years ago. He just reports his position again. Adrian watches the living body on the screen and understands it clearly: danger makes him want to touch Roman more, not run.

else.why: The photo from when they were seventeen

ja.hint: At the lock screen, his hand hovers over the switch. The man outside is waiting for one sentence. Send him back, let him in, or don't hang up yet?

opts.t: Don't plan around me. Walk me through the route.
then: Adrian props his phone next to the lock screen. With both feeds lit side by side, he realizes he's been watching only Roman, not the hallway behind him.
I can't see the right side of the frame. What's there?
Service room. From your end, there's no way to confirm it's empty.
So you're not safe just because I can see you.

One word, and his urge to handle everything himself goes quiet. He has the duty desk state the verified fallback route first, then has Roman repeat the next step back. No jargon. Just where to go, when to stop, and who confirms.

Roman backs off behind the solid wall as instructed. The second that broad shape leaves the frame, Adrian's hand clenches. He almost calls him back. Not out of fear. It's that in the one second the body is off-screen, there's a hole in his chest.
Inside the safe zone. Didn't enter the service room.
I'm in the safe zone. Adrian, I'm still here.

The words go straight from the earpiece into his ear, low and steady, with the hum of Roman's chest behind them. Adrian holds the talk button and closes his eyes and lets them stay in his ear half a second longer. He doesn't open the door. For the first time, he doesn't treat the closed door as proof that he can't do anything.
opts.rthink: He asked about the route, not me. ...That's better. He's finally stopped standing in the doorway for me.

opts.t: Don't come in tonight. Get your relief to the duty desk.
then: Is that not coming into this apartment tonight, or not running your personal security anymore?
The first one. The second, we discuss tomorrow. In writing.
The question is so precise it makes it harder for Adrian to stay angry. Like even a refusal only counts if Roman catches it gracefully.
You don't have to act like you understand me this well.
Roman turns his head and tells the relief to report to the duty desk and send over a badge number. Adrian's phone gets no long explanation.

Just the handoff location, the confirmation time, the next security notice. Those few lines are colder than any "I'm worried about you," and they make him want to reach out and touch the man who sent them.
He regrets it as soon as it's out. Roman doesn't use it as a reason to walk back to the door.
You told me not to come in tonight. I'm doing what you said.

The elevator doors open again. The steel slides shut over that familiar shoulder a little at a time. The shirt catches the light once more, then it's gone. He wanted distance. Now that he has it, his body isn't happy. Like someone pulled something warm out of his hand, leaving only empty, and an itch.
He presses the phone to the cold door and leaves it there a long time before he pulls it back. The cold of the door doesn't touch the heat in his fingertips.
opts.rthink: He said "tonight." Not "from now on." ...I can hear the difference. I'm right downstairs. I'm not going anywhere.

opts.t: Come in after the passage is cleared. Don't touch me tonight.
then: Passage confirmation pops up on the lock screen. Adrian double-checks with the duty desk before he slides the chain.
